<STRUCT_0001>
A more standard case of the above lemma is the following.
(The version with ``flat'' follows from
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0001>.)

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme. Let
<MATH_0002>
be a commutative diagram of morphisms of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0003>.
Assume that <MATH_0004> is surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation
and assume that <MATH_0005> is locally of finite presentation (resp.<SPACE_0001>locally
of finite type). Then <MATH_0006> is locally of finite presentation
(resp.<SPACE_0002>locally of finite type).

Since <MATH_0001> is an fppf covering, it induces a surjection of
fppf sheaves (Topologies on Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0001>) and the
lemma is a special case of Lemma <REF_0002>.
On the other hand, an easier argument is to deduce it from
the analogue for schemes. Namely, the problem is <ACCENT_0001>tale local
on <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> (Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas
<REF_0003> and
<REF_0004>).
Hence we may assume that <MATH_0004> and <MATH_0005> are affine
schemes. Since <MATH_0006> is open
(Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0005>),
we can choose an affine
scheme <MATH_0007> and an <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism <MATH_0008> such that the
composition <MATH_0009> is surjective. In this case the result
follows from Descent, Lemma
<REF_0006>.
